message.content:
Build an **admin Backups UI** for the Nxeon platform at /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + Prisma + Postgres + serial job worker). Admins need a fleet-wide view of every server's backups, with restore visibility.

## Current state (verified by a mapping pass — these facts are reliable)
- There is NO `app/admin/backups` dir and NO admin/aggregate backup UI. Backups are Proxmox `vzdump` archives on the `backup` storage — there is NO DB Backup table; enumeration is a live Proxmox call.
- Primitives in `lib/proxmox.ts` (READ-ONLY, do not edit this file): `listBackups(vmid?)` reads the env-primary node's `backup` storage content; `listBackupsOn(client, vmid)` takes an explicit pve client (multi-node capable) and returns `StorageBackupEntry[]` (volid, ctime, size); `nodeTargets()` in `lib/monitoring.ts` yields all enabled nodes' clients. `lib/monitoring.ts` `backupSummary()` already iterates all nodeTargets reading each node's backup storage (counts + newest/oldest only) — a good reference for the multi-node loop.
- Backups are keyed by vmid inside the volid — map archive→owner by joining vmid back to a `Server` row (`Server.vmid`). The admin monitoring page already does a vmid→Server join (`byVmid`, app/admin/monitoring/page.tsx:58) — mirror that.
- Existing CUSTOMER backup code to model the UX on: `lib/actions-server-ops.ts` `listServerBackups(serverId)` + `requestRestore(serverId, volid)` (ownership-scoped); `lib/actions-server.ts` `createBackup(serverId)` (enqueues BACKUP_CREATE) + `getBackupJob(serverId)` (progress); client components `components/customer/BackupRestore.tsx`, `BackupControls.tsx`, `BackupSchedule.tsx`. `Server` fields: `autoBackup`, `backupIntervalHours`, `lastAutoBackup`. `lib/backup-verify.ts` has `backupScheduleHealth({...})` → a health sentence.
- JobType has `BACKUP_CREATE`/`BACKUP_RESTORE`; the worker handlers (backupCreate, backupRestore) already exist — you enqueue jobs, you do NOT write worker code.

## What to build
- `app/admin/backups/page.tsx` — server component, gated `await requireArea("fleet")` (import from `@/lib/rbac`; follow the structure of `app/admin/nodes/page.tsx`: `export const dynamic="force-dynamic"`, fetch server-side, delegate interactivity to client components, use `@/components/ui/primitives`). Show a fleet-wide table: every backup archive across ALL nodes, joined to its owning Server (customer email, hostname, vmid), with age (ctime), size, and node. Include per-server backup-schedule health (autoBackup on/off, interval, lastAutoBackup, `backupScheduleHealth`). Summarize at top: total archives, total size, servers with NO recent backup (a real risk signal), oldest/newest.
- `lib/actions-backups-admin.ts` (new, `"use server"`, ADMIN-gated) — `listAllBackups()`: loop `nodeTargets()`, call `listBackupsOn(client)` per node, join each archive's vmid to a Server (include orphans whose vmid has no Server row — flag them). An ADMIN restore action `adminRequestRestore(serverId, volid)` that validates the volid really belongs to that server's vmid then enqueues `BACKUP_RESTORE` (payload {volid}) + writes an AuditLog. An ADMIN `adminCreateBackup(serverId)` enqueuing `BACKUP_CREATE` + AuditLog. Restore is destructive — the UI must confirm.
- `components/admin/BackupsAdmin.tsx` (+ any sub-components) — client table with filters (by server, by node, orphans), a restore control with a hard confirm ("this overwrites the live VM"), and a create-backup button with progress.
- `test/backups-admin.test.ts` — tests that bite.

## Files you OWN (only these)
- `app/admin/backups/**`
- `components/admin/BackupsAdmin.tsx` (+ sub-components under components/admin/backups/** if you want)
- `lib/actions-backups-admin.ts`
- `test/backups-admin*.test.ts`

## Files you must NOT touch (put instructions in your report)
- `lib/proxmox.ts`, `lib/monitoring.ts`, `lib/backup-verify.ts` (read-only imports only)
- `lib/admin-groups.ts` — the admin nav. I will add the Backups entry. In your report, give me the EXACT entry to add: which section (it belongs in `fleet` → likely alongside the `operations` entry Monitoring/Jobs), the label ("Backups"), an icon name (check the icons map in `components/portal/Shell.tsx` for a fitting existing icon — e.g. an archive/database icon), and the href `/admin/backups`.
- `lib/rbac.ts` — I will add `/admin/backups` → `fleet` to `HREF_AREA`. (Confirm fleet is right.)
- `prisma/schema.prisma` (frozen — no new model; backups stay live-from-Proxmox), `worker/index.ts`.

## Platform rules (non-negotiable)
- `"use server"` = every export is a public endpoint. `lib/actions-backups-admin.ts` exports must `requireArea("fleet")` (or stricter) INSIDE each function — an admin restore that isn't gated is a cross-tenant data-destruction hole. The restore action MUST re-validate the volid belongs to the target server's vmid (never trust a client-supplied volid) — a recycled/mismatched volid restoring the wrong archive onto a VM is exactly the class of bug this platform has been burned by.
- Honesty: if a node is unreachable when enumerating, SHOW that node as "couldn't enumerate" rather than silently omitting its backups (a silently-missing node reads as "this server has no backups" — dangerous). Never claim a backup exists that Proxmox didn't return.
- Tests must bite: use `stripCommentsAndStrings`/`stripComments` from `test/_source-tools.ts` for source tripwires asserting every action authenticates + the restore re-validates volid ownership. Unit-test the archive→Server vmid-join and the "servers with no recent backup" computation as pure functions (factor them out).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for your files; `npm test` (node:test).
- Do NOT run prisma db push/migrate, next build in place, git commit, deploy, systemctl.

## Deliver
Typechecking code + tests. Final report: (1) the exact `lib/admin-groups.ts` nav entry (section, label, icon, href) + confirm the icon exists in Shell.tsx's icon map; (2) confirm `/admin/backups` → `fleet` for HREF_AREA; (3) what's real vs simulated (in NXEON_SANDBOX, does listBackups return anything? note it); (4) test count. Report is data for me.

import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
import { realUser } from "./auth";

/**
 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
 *
 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
 */
export type Area =
  | "overview"
  | "analytics"
  | "clients"
  | "support"
  | "fleet"
  | "billing"
  | "platform";

/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  platform: ["ADMIN"],
};

export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
}

/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
}

/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {
  "/admin": "overview",
  "/admin/analytics": "analytics",
  "/admin/users": "clients",
  "/admin/support": "support",
  "/admin/servers": "fleet",
  "/admin/nodes": "fleet",
  "/admin/ips": "fleet",
  "/admin/provisioning": "fleet",
  "/admin/jobs": "fleet",
  "/admin/monitoring": "fleet",
  "/admin/abuse": "fleet",
  "/admin/infrastructure": "fleet",
  "/admin/subscriptions": "billing",
  "/admin/billing": "billing",
  "/admin/invoices": "billing",
  "/admin/plans": "billing",
  "/admin/coupons": "billing",
  "/admin/game-plans": "billing",
  "/admin/gift-codes": "billing",
  "/admin/email-plans": "billing",
  "/admin/products": "billing",
  "/admin/affiliate": "billing",
  "/admin/testimonials": "platform",
  "/admin/feedback": "support",
  "/admin/chat": "support",
  "/admin/mail": "platform",
  "/admin/orgs": "clients",
  "/admin/visitors": "analytics",
  "/admin/logs": "platform",
  "/admin/newsletter": "platform",
  "/admin/domains": "platform",
  "/admin/grant": "platform",
  "/admin/audit": "platform",
  "/admin/automation": "platform",
  "/admin/settings": "platform",
  "/admin/staff": "platform",
  "/admin/email-templates": "platform",
  "/admin/games": "platform",
  "/admin/blog": "platform",
};

export function areaForHref(href: string): Area {
  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";
}

export function canAccessHref(role: Role, href: string): boolean {
  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));
}

/**
 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
 */
export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
  const user = await realUser();
  if (!user) redirect("/login");
  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
  return user;
}

### (3) Real vs simulated (NXEON_SANDBOX)
Backup **enumeration is REAL, never simulated.** `listBackups`, `listBackupsOn`, and the `/storage/backup/content` GET in `lib/proxmox.ts` have **no** `SANDBOX` branch — only `getGuestDiskUsage` and the worker's create/restore *execution* simulate. So `listAllBackups()` makes live Proxmox reads regardless of sandbox: if a real Proxmox answers (as on this host), it returns real archives; if a node is unreachable, that node is reported `reachable: false` ("couldn't enumerate") and never silently dropped. The BACKUP_CREATE / BACKUP_RESTORE jobs I enqueue are executed by the existing worker handlers, which DO simulate in sandbox (see `worker/restore.ts` SANDBOX branch).

### Implementation notes for you
- **Why I read `/storage/backup/content` directly instead of `listBackupsOn(client)` for enumeration:** `listBackupsOn(client, vmid)` filters to a single vmid, so it structurally *cannot* surface orphan archives (vmids with no Server row) — and orphans are a required signal. I read the same read-only endpoint `listBackupsOn`/`backupSummary` call internally, per node, via `nodeTargets()`. `listBackupsOn` **is** used for the authoritative re-validation in `adminRequestRestore`, built through `pveFor(server.node)` so a server pinned to a non-primary node is checked against its own node (vmids collide across nodes).
